extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting papers to EMNLP 2025 and subsequent ACL conferences
extracted.subtask_description: Announces that the Responsible NLP Research Checklist must be completed by authors and will be published as an appendix for accepted EMNLP 2025 (and subsequent ACL) papers; explains practical and procedural implications for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible NLP Research Checklist (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible NLP Research Checklist - it has been part of ARR submissions for some time now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist covers several areas (see individual items). The checklist has been used during review; filling it out incorrectly or misleadingly can result in desk rejection. For EMNLP 2025 and subsequent ACL conferences, the completed checklist will be published alongside accepted papers as an appendix. Checklists do not count against page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: How you collected and annotated data
rubrics_metrics.description: How you collected and annotated data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should describe data collection and annotation procedures clearly and thoroughly on the checklist; because the checklist will be public, be extra careful and thorough when completing this section. Inaccurate or misleading answers can lead to desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: What datasets you used and their limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: What datasets you used and their limitations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should list datasets used and explicitly state limitations. Publication of the checklist will make dataset choices and acknowledged limitations visible to the broader community, encouraging transparency and careful consideration of dataset issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Your training and evaluation setup
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details about model training and evaluation (e.g., splits, hyperparameters, evaluation procedures). Because checklist responses are used during review and will be public if accepted, be precise and complete about experimental setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential impacts of your work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should describe potential positive and negative impacts of their research. Public checklist appendices aim to increase transparency about ethical and societal considerations, which may influence community understanding of risks and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational costs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report computational resources and costs associated with experiments. Given public availability of checklists, documenting computational footprint helps transparency around environmental and resource considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist completeness, accuracy, and public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Your checklist responses will be public if your paper is accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must be careful and thorough when completing the checklist because responses become public appendices for accepted papers. Checklists do not count against page limits. Misleading or incorrect answers have been and can be treated as grounds for desk rejection; the policy encourages truthful, comprehensive reporting to improve transparency.
